transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07 10:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Gomez (Orion - Head of ML), Ethan Park (Orion - Platform Eng), Nina Rao (Orion - Security), Tom Alvarez (Orion - Product)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in, model selection and pinning, go/no-go criteria for pilot phase.

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:04] Laura Gomez: yes, loud and clear, thanks Maya.
[00:07] Samir Patel: morning all, Samir here, I'll run through the perf slides and the benchmark notes.
[00:12] Ethan Park: quick note we have dev cluster free from 2pm if you want to run any heavy tests later.
[00:16] Nina Rao: I'll be listening in for security questions, thanks.

[00:30] Samir Patel: ok so slide one, we've got the latest runs comparing rdx-2.3-prod, rdx-2.2-stable and one open baseline (lmb-v1), results are in the shared sheet link in the chat. rdx-2.3 shows a 12% latency improvement p50 across our sample but 6% higher token cost due to slightly larger output lengths, so throughput wins but unit cost tradeoff is...
[00:55] Laura Gomez: wait can you repeat the cost bit? We saw token cost go up on rdx-2.3?
[00:58] Samir Patel: yeah, so because temperature and stop sequences produce slightly longer outputs in our product-summary route, total token output increased. We can tune decoding params to match rdx-2.2 behavior, but out-of-the-box the latency is better and quality is slightly improved on entity extraction.
[01:20] Tom Alvarez: quality improvements are what we care about, but cost is a gating factor for us, especially on high volume product pages.

[01:45] Maya Chen: right, and that's exactly where pinning and fallback policies come in - you can pin the route to rdx-2.3 and then have an automatic fallback to rdx-2.2 or a quantized variant during peak if latency spikes or cost thresholds are exceeded.
[02:05] Ethan Park: question on routing: how hard is it to set a rule that routes 10% to cheaper variant for A/B? Can we do that via API or only via console?
[02:12] Samir Patel: you can do it both ways; API supports percentage rollouts, and console gives a visual canary. We'll share the JSON snippet later.

[02:40] Nina Rao: from a security standpoint we need to know whether KMS keys can be customer-managed and whether logs include token IDs but not content - last time we saw partial logs, is that still the case?
[02:52] Maya Chen: yes, private deployments support customer-managed KMS/HSM. For hosted, we offer envelope encryption with customer KMS integrations for enterprise plans. Audit logs redact user prompt content by default but include token-level metadata, timestamps, and route identifiers. We'll drop SOC2 and network topology docs in the doc bucket.

[03:20] Samir Patel: going back to model selection - we also trialed a quantized rdx-2.3-q8 for throughput; it cuts token cost by ~22% but the entity extraction F1 drops ~1.8 points on the evaluation set. For Orion's SLA, do you have a minimum quality threshold?
[03:42] Laura Gomez: we'd like to stay within 1 point F1 of the baseline for launch, so that might make q8 risky unless we can tune prompts.

[04:00] Tom Alvarez: could fallback be to q8 during traffic spikes and otherwise use full fp16 rdx-2.3? That might balance cost and quality.
[04:08] Samir Patel: yes that's a common pattern; Redwood supports rule-based fallback e.g., if p95 latency > 800ms or error rate > 1% then fallback to rdx-2.3-q8 or rdx-2.2. You can chain fallbacks too.

[04:30] Ethan Park: latency targets - what was the p95 on the dev benchmark? I saw p50 but not p95.
[04:36] Samir Patel: p95 for rdx-2.3 on your sample is about 820ms on the dev GPU pool, rdx-2.2 p95 is ~980ms. Quantized q8 p95 is ~700ms but remember the quality tradeoff.

[05:05] Laura Gomez: ok so rdx-2.3 seems promising. Next question: model pinning lifecycle - how do we handle rollbacks if a new pinned version degrades in production?
[05:12] Maya Chen: you can set automatic rollback rules tied to evaluation metrics and SLO breaches; for example, if generated quality (measured by your eval harness) drops >2 points on a rolling 24h window, Redwood can automatically rollback to previous pinned version. We also recommend a canary period of 24-72h with 5-10% traffic.

[05:45] Nina Rao: is the evaluation harness something Redwood runs or do we supply prompts?
[05:49] Samir Patel: both - you can provide your prompt set and Redwood will run periodic quality regression checks against pinned models; we can also hook into your CI to run the tests before promoting.

[06:10] Tom Alvarez: what about audit trails - we need an immutable record of any pin or rollback event for compliance.
[06:16] Maya Chen: those are logged in the audit trail with user, timestamp, diff of config, and we can export them to your SIEM via webhook or S3.

[06:40] Ethan Park: on sandbox tests, last week's run showed some flakiness due to our dev infra, Samir, you mentioned using a dedicated reserved pool would be more stable?
[06:50] Samir Patel: yes, Dedicated gives you reserved GPU capacity which reduces noisy neighbor effects. For pilot phase, a small dedicated pool plus burst capacity tends to give consistent p95s. Pricing sheet will show the commit required.

[07:10] Laura Gomez: price sensitivity: what is the delta between hosted usage and a small dedicated commit? ballpark numbers?
[07:17] Maya Chen: i'll send exact numbers in the pricing sheet, but qualitatively, dedicated reduces per-token cost by 20-35% depending on utilization and gives predictable throughput.

[07:40] Samir Patel: quick demo of the pin config - (screen) here is the route config: route "/product-summary" pinned to rdx-2.3-prod, canary 10% to rdx-2.3-q8, fallback chain: rdx-2.2-stable -> rdx-2.3-q8. You can set metrics: max p95 ms, error rate threshold, and cost per 1M tokens triggers.

[08:10] (audio: typing)
[08:20] Laura Gomez: question about tokenization differences - we saw slightly different token counts between rdx-2.2 and rdx-2.3, is that a model change or tokenizer?
[08:25] Samir Patel: it's the tokenizer update in 2.3, we tightened whitespace handling, so token counts drop for some inputs and increase for others; that explains some of the cost variance.

[08:50] Nina Rao: for our legal/compliance review we need to see data retention policies and the ability to disable any persistent caching of prompts in hosted mode. Can we do that?
[09:00] Maya Chen: yes, you can disable prefix caching at the route level; for hosted enterprise we also offer data residency controls and log retention tunables. We'll include the doc links.

[09:20] Tom Alvarez: action item: can we run a 10k sample on dev with rdx-2.3 pinned and q8 fallback to see actual cost delta?
[09:26] Samir Patel: yes I can run that today if Ethan can provide the sample dataset and access to the dev cluster.

[09:40] Ethan Park: I'll drop the dataset in the shared bucket and grant Samir access after this call.

[10:00] (timestamp skip)
[10:15] Samir Patel: quick note on the rollback process - if you trigger a manual rollback we keep the previous config as history and we can replay traffic segments for debugging. Also our SDK returns a model_version header so you can attribute responses to model IDs in logs.

[10:35] Laura Gomez: about A/B testing: we want to measure user engagement impact, what's the recommended traffic split and minimum sample size?
[10:40] Maya Chen: depends on effect size; for small UI copy changes we'd suggest at least 5k impressions per arm; for model-level changes where you expect small deltas, aim for 20-50k impressions. We can help set up experiment dashboards.

[11:05] Nina Rao: any blockers from security side right now? we need the KMS integration details and SIEM webhook formats.
[11:10] Maya Chen: we'll send the KMS integration guide and example webhook payloads; Samir will attach the audit log schema.

[11:30] Tom Alvarez: can we get a tentative timeline to go from pilot to launch? assuming we pin rdx-2.3 next week and run the tests?
[11:37] Maya Chen: typical pilot -> launch for this scope is 6-8 weeks, assuming no major compliance roadblocks and a 2-3 week canary. We can compress timelines if you opt for a bigger dedicated commit and run parallel benchmarks.

[11:55] (wrap-up)
[11:56] Maya Chen: ok recap: action items are Samir to run 10k dev benchmark, Maya to send pricing and SOC2 docs, Nina to provide KMS questions, and Laura/Ethan to confirm sample dataset and accept dev access. We'll aim to pin /product-summary to rdx-2.3 for canary next Tue pending results.
[12:10] Laura Gomez: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[12:12] Ethan Park: thanks, bye.
[12:13] Maya Chen: thanks all, bye.
